subject: botany_2
question_text: Name the bacteria which is a common inhabitant of the human intestine. How is it used in biotechnology?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.41, printed question 74. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Escherichia coli is the answer to both halves, but the second half needs the WORD 'vector' or 'host', not just the name again.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The bacterium
steps.margin_note: Full name, location, and one line on what it does there.
lines: ESCHERICHIA COLI (E. coli) is a common inhabitant
It lives harmlessly in the large intestine and
helps in the production of some vitamins.
steps.why: A bacterium that already lives safely in people is easy and cheap to grow, which is part of why it became the standard laboratory organism.
common_mistakes: Spelling it Escherichia coly. The species is Escherichia COLI.
Saying it is always harmful. Most strains are harmless residents.
steps.memory_tip: A gut resident that became the laboratory workhorse.

steps.label: Its use
steps.margin_note: Say host, say vector, and say why speed matters. Do not merge the two roles.

lines.text: The standard HOST in rDNA technology

lines: E. coli is used as the HOST ORGANISM in
Its plasmids, such as pBR322, are used as CLONING
It multiplies quickly, so a cloned gene is copied
many times in a few hours.
steps.why: A host that divides every twenty minutes turns one recombinant cell into millions overnight, which is what makes gene cloning practical.
common_mistakes: Saying E. coli is itself a plasmid. It is a BACTERIUM; its plasmids are the vectors.
Giving the name without any use. The second half is a whole mark.
steps.memory_tip: The bacterium is the host; its plasmid is the vector.
